dishes.text: Delicious smash burgers with an optional egg

recipe.title: Double Smash Burgers with Crispy Onion Edges and an Optional Fried Egg
recipe.description: Two craggy, lace-edged beef patties per bun, each draped in melted American cheese, stacked on a butter-toasted bun with cold lettuce, tomato, pickles and a tangy house burger sauce — with a runny-yolk fried egg on top for anyone who wants it.

ingredients.item: Iceberg lettuce, outer leaves removed, 6 large inner leaves (new buy)
Onions, white, peeled and sliced paper-thin
Tomatoes, cored and cut into 6 mm slices

steps.title: Mix the burger sauce
steps.content: In a small bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, ketchup, yellow mustard, sweet relish, onion powder, paprika and garlic salt until smooth and evenly pink. Taste and adjust with salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate until serving — it gets better as it sits.

steps.title: Set up the cold garnishes
steps.content: Arrange the 6 large lettuce leaves, the sliced tomatoes and the drained pickle chips on a platter. Season the tomato slices lightly with salt and pepper. Keep the thinly sliced white onion in a separate small bowl — it goes onto the raw patties, not onto the platter. Refrigerate the platter so the lettuce and tomato stay cold and crisp against the hot patties.

steps.title: Portion the raw beef
steps.content: Divide the raw ground beef into 12 loose balls of about 90 g each. Roll them just enough to hold together — do not pack or knead them; compressed meat will not spread into those crisp lace edges. Set the balls on a tray, cover, and keep refrigerated until the pan is screaming hot. Do not salt them yet.

steps.title: Butter and toast the buns
steps.content: Split the 6 buns and spread the softened butter over all 12 cut faces. Heat a large heavy skillet over medium (5 on the dial) and toast the buns cut-side down in batches, 60–90 seconds each, until deep golden. Set them on a sheet pan, cut side up, and keep them near the stove.

steps.title: Get the pan ripping hot
steps.content: Wipe the skillet clean and set it over high heat (9–10) for a full 5 minutes until it is just beginning to smoke. Add 1 tablespoon of the avocado oil and swirl to coat. A properly overheated pan is the entire secret to a smash burger crust — if it is not smoking, wait.

steps.title: Smash the first batch
steps.content: Place 3 or 4 raw beef balls in the dry-hot pan, well spaced, and immediately press each one flat and thin with a sturdy metal spatula (back it with a second spatula or a heavy pan lid for leverage), holding the press for 10 seconds. Season the tops with salt and pepper and scatter a small pinch of the thin-sliced onion onto each patty, pressing it in lightly. Cook undisturbed 90 seconds to 2 minutes, until the edges are dark brown and lacy. Do not crowd the pan.

steps.title: Flip, cheese and stack
steps.content: Scrape hard under each patty with the spatula so the entire crust lifts, flip, and lay a slice of American cheese on each. Cook 45–60 seconds more, then stack one patty on top of another right in the pan so the cheese welds them together. Transfer each double to a waiting toasted bun bottom. Repeat steps 6 and 7 with the remaining beef in two more batches, adding the second tablespoon of avocado oil only if the pan looks dry.

steps.title: Fry the optional eggs
steps.content: Pour off all but a thin film of the beef fat, lower the heat to medium-low (3–4), and crack in the eggs one per guest who wants one. Season with salt and pepper and fry 2–3 minutes until the whites are fully set and the yolks are still liquid. Slide one egg onto each burger that is getting one.

steps.title: Build and serve immediately
steps.content: Spread a heavy spoonful of burger sauce on each toasted bun top. Top the stacked patties with a lettuce leaf, tomato slices and pickle chips, crown with the bun top, and press gently. Serve right away while the crust is still crisp and the yolk is still running — smash burgers wait for nobody.

recipe.notes: Protein per serving: about 53 g (with the egg). Calories per serving: about 1140 (with the egg); about 1070 without. New buys: 80/20 ground chuck, potato buns, American cheese, butter, iceberg lettuce, dill pickle chips, mayonnaise, yellow mustard. Make-ahead: the burger sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead and actually improves overnight; slice the onion, tomato and lettuce a few hours ahead and keep them chilled and covered. Pro tips — keep the beef balls cold right up to the moment they hit the pan so they smash thin without sticking to the spatula; press each patty only once, in the first 10 seconds, or you squeeze out the juice with no crust to show for it; scrape with a stiff metal spatula at a low angle so the browned crust comes up with the meat instead of staying in the pan; work in three batches and never crowd the skillet, or the patties steam instead of searing. Leftovers: keep patties and buns separate in the fridge up to 2 days and revive the patties in the Tovala on Steam 3 minutes then Broil 1 minute; toast the buns fresh.

dishes.text: Either you can think of something, or nothing

recipe.title: Either You Can Think of Something, or Nothing
recipe.description: Craggy smashed baby potatoes roasted until the edges shatter like chips, drenched in garlic butter, blistered under parmesan, and finished with lemon and parsley so every piece tastes like the crispy corner of the pan.

ingredients.item: Baby potatoes (The Little Potato Co.), scrubbed, left whole
Salt (for the boiling water and for seasoning)

ingredients.amount: 45 g, plus a little extra for the pan

ingredients.item: Parsley, fresh, leaves finely chopped, stems discarded (new buy)
Lemon, raw — zested, then halved for juice (new buy)

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.content: Put the scrubbed whole baby potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by 5 cm, and salt the water heavily (it should taste like a good soup). Bring to a boil over high heat (9–10), then drop to a simmer (3–4) and cook 18–20 minutes, until a paring knife slides into the biggest potato with zero resistance. Underboiled potatoes will not smash — they crumble or bounce, so err on the tender side.

steps.title: Drain and steam-dry
steps.content: Drain the potatoes in a colander and let them sit, uncovered, for 5 minutes. The surface moisture flashes off and that dry skin is what turns crisp later. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 230°C / 450°F and lightly oil a large sheet pan with olive oil.

steps.title: Make the garlic butter
steps.content: In a small saucepan over low heat (2–3), melt the 115 g butter with the 45 g olive oil and the 2 tablespoons minced garlic. Warm gently 2–3 minutes, swirling, just until the garlic smells sweet and the butter is fully liquid — do not let the garlic take on color or it will turn bitter in the oven. Stir in the 1 teaspoon dried oregano and pull off the heat.

steps.title: Smash
steps.content: Arrange the warm potatoes on the oiled sheet pan with space between each one. Press each potato flat with the bottom of a heavy glass or a measuring cup until it's about 1.5 cm thick and the edges split and fray — those ragged edges are the crispy part, so don't chase neat discs. Work in a single layer; use two pans if they crowd.

steps.title: Butter and season
steps.content: Spoon or brush about half the garlic butter over the smashed potatoes, getting it into the cracks. Season generously with salt and pepper on top.

steps.title: Roast
steps.content: Roast on the oven's upper-middle rack at 230°C / 450°F for 25 minutes, until the undersides are deep gold and the edges are visibly crisp. Rotate the pan front-to-back once at the halfway mark for even color. Don't flip them — the flat bottom is doing the work.

steps.title: Butter again, then parmesan
steps.content: Pull the pan out. Spoon the remaining garlic butter over the potatoes, scraping in all the garlic solids from the pan, then scatter the 60 g grated parmesan evenly over the top.

steps.title: Broil to finish
steps.content: Switch the oven to broil and return the pan to the top rack for 3–4 minutes, until the parmesan is melted and browned in patches. Stand at the oven and watch it — at this distance it goes from golden to burnt in under a minute.

steps.title: Dress and serve
steps.content: Slide the potatoes onto a warm platter. Zest the lemon over the top, then squeeze about half the lemon's juice over everything. Shower with the chopped parsley, add a final pinch of salt and a few grinds of pepper, and serve immediately while the edges are still shattering-crisp.

recipe.notes: Protein per serving: about 8 g. Calories per serving: about 405. New buys: unsalted butter, freshly grated parmesan, fresh parsley, 1 lemon. Make-ahead: boil and smash the potatoes up to 6 hours ahead, leave them buttered on the sheet pan at room temperature, then roast right before guests sit down — the second half of the butter, the parmesan and the broil all happen à la minute. Pro tips: salt the boiling water aggressively, since it's the only chance to season the inside of the potato; give each potato breathing room on the pan, because a crowded pan steams instead of crisping; and add the lemon juice only at the table — do it early and the crust softens. Leftovers keep 3 days covered in the fridge and come back to life in the air fryer at 200°C / 400°F for 5–6 minutes in a single layer.
